titleEn: While We Wait, Draw in the Dirt!

pages.text: "When is Mom's boat coming?" Mina stamped at the landing. Mom had crossed to the market that morning. Low water left dry soil all the way to the landing.
"I'll wait here. I want to see her boat first." Mina sat on dry ground far from the water. Experienced eldest Raju sat beside them.
No boat showed across the river. Mina kept asking, "Still far? Still?" "Far," Raju answered for the tenth time.
Raju picked up two dry twigs and gave Mina one. "While We Wait, Draw in the Dirt!" "What's that?" Mina accepted it.
Raju drew a long boat. "Mom's boat looks like this, right?" Mina drew wavy water beneath it.
Now Mina's turn. A boatman appeared aboard. "He rows, stroke, stroke!" Rowing sounds came naturally from Mina's mouth.
They drew in turns: Raju a jar, Mina green fruit. "Will Mom buy these, too?" Their picture stretched across the dry ground.
Then came rowing sounds. A boat reached the landing, and Mom stepped off. Mina waved beside the drawing. "Look here!"
Mom crouched before it. "A rower here, too?" Mina pointed with the twig. "It's your boat!"
Mom hugged Mina tightly. Mina snuggled in. "I drew with Raju while waiting."
